alternate_names: Arulmigu Moorthivinayagar Temple, Manimoortheeswaram (HR & CE Department name)
deities: Uchishta Ganapati (one of the 32 forms of Ganesha) with 4 hands, holding Goddess Neelavani (Neelasaraswathi) on his left lap; his trunk rests on her navel, symbolising the divinity of pregnancy - the deity is especially worshipped by couples seeking progeny

Other shrines: Nellaiappar (Shiva), Gandhimathi Amman, Subramaniya with Valli and Deivanai, Dakshinamurthy, Chandikeswarar, Swarna Akarshana Bhairavar, sages Patanjali and Vyagrabathar, and 31 forms of Ganesha

history.dynasty: Not firmly documented; dated to around 1000 CE by temple tradition
history.period: About 1000 years old (founded ~1000 AD per temple tradition and several sources) - inscriptional verification pending
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV lists the town as Tirunelveli, but the temple stands in the MANIMOORTHEESWARAM neighbourhood of Tirunelveli (Manimoorthispuram, Tirunelveli 627001), on the banks of the Thamirabarani river, about 2 km from Tirunelveli Junction - documented with the corrected town. This is the biggest Uchishta Ganapati temple in Asia per Wikipedia and local claims (claim repeated widely but unsourced - verify). Uchishta Ganapati is one of the 32 forms of Vinayagar; the HR & CE Department recognises the temple as 'Arulmigu Moorthivinayagar Temple, Manimoortheeswaram' (temple number TM038972). The shrine has a five-tiered rajagopuram and a large complex; visitors note its calming, spacious surroundings. The sacred tanks are Rishi Theertham (of the Thamirabarani) and Ruthrapath Theertham; the sthala virukshas are the Vanni tree and the palmyrah tree. The temple is famous for blessing couples with children. Narrow approach roads and poor signposting make it tricky to locate - use coordinates.

name: Uchishta Ganapathy Temple
town_description: Manimoortheeswaram is a riverside neighbourhood in Tirunelveli town on the Thamirabarani river, near Tirunelveli Junction. It is a quiet residential area whose best-known landmark is the Uchishta Ganapathy temple, about 1.86 km from Palayamkottai railway station.

travel.airport: Tuticorin Airport is the nearest domestic airport (verify distance).
travel.railway: Tirunelveli Junction, about 2 km; Palayamkottai railway station is about 1.86 km from the temple.
travel.road: Manimoorthispuram, Junction, Tirunelveli 627001; narrow lanes - autos or taxis from the Junction are the easiest option.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March. The 10-day Vinayagar Chathurthi and Tamil New Year draw the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: Justdial lists only a morning session 7:00 AM to 12:00 PM daily, while a place listing shows 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM - verify locally before visiting.
